domains.name: Kain Standard Library
domains.label: Kain Stdlib
domains.description: Navigate Kain's massive standard library â€” 65+ modules, 3500+ public symbols. List modules, inspect symbols, read signatures and docs, view source code, and explore the full keyword reference.
domains.promptSnippet: Query Kain stdlib modules, symbols, docs, keywords, and source
promptGuidelines: Use kain_stdlib for all Kain standard library lookups â€” finding symbols, checking function signatures, reading source, and looking up language keywords.
For semantic code search over real Kain examples, use the kain_examples tool instead.

list_modules.label: List Modules
list_modules.description: List all Kain stdlib modules with public/private symbol counts and source paths.

get_symbols.label: Get Module Symbols
get_symbols.description: List all symbols defined in a specific Kain stdlib module (e.g. 'math', 'os').

search_symbols.label: Search Symbols
search_symbols.description: Fuzzy-search Kain stdlib symbols by name, signature, or docs across the entire standard library or within a specific module.

get_details.label: Get Symbol Details
get_details.description: Get full documentation, signature, kind, and location for any stdlib symbol.

get_source.label: Get Symbol Source
get_source.description: Read the actual Kain source code implementation of any stdlib function, struct, or actor.

list_keywords.label: List Keywords
list_keywords.description: Full Kain language keyword reference â€” compiler-owned semantic constructs (world, entangle, teleport, etc.) plus standard keywords.

get_keyword.label: Get Keyword Help
get_keyword.description: Detailed help for any specific Kain keyword: syntax models, descriptions, usage examples.

domains.name: Kain Bazel
domains.label: Kain Bazel
domains.description: Build, test, and manage the Kain repo with Bazel â€” compile targets, run test suites, manage the Bazel server lifecycle, sync native runtime build files, and check binary freshness.
domains.promptSnippet: Build, test, and manage the Kain Bazel build system
promptGuidelines: Use kain_bazel for all Bazel operations: building the compiler, running smoke tests, managing server lifecycle, syncing runtime builds, and checking binary staleness.

build.label: Build
build.description: Build any Bazel target. Common presets: //:kain (compiler CLI), //:kn (launcher), //runtime:all (native runtime), //:kain --config=release.

test.label: Test
test.description: Run any Bazel test target. Common: //:developer_smoke_tests, //:crate_tests, //:key_crate_tests, //runtime:native_runtime_tests.

server.label: Server
server.description: Manage the Bazel server lifecycle: status (check if alive), start (warm up), stop (shutdown), restart (cycle). A cold server adds 30-90s startup cost.

sync.label: Sync
sync.description: Check or regenerate native runtime Bazel build files. 'check' validates no drift; 'sync' regenerates from runtime/native manifests.

binary_age.label: Binary Age
binary_age.description: Check when the kain/kn binaries were last built and compare against the latest source commit. Detects stale binaries that need rebuilding.

freshness.label: Freshness
freshness.description: Full repo freshness audit: Bazel server status + binary age vs source + native runtime sync status + last git commit. Single go/no-go signal.

domains.name: Kain Language
domains.label: Kain Lang
domains.description: Compile, check, run, and test Kain source files and projects â€” LLVM native builds, workspace compilation, smoke tests, and GPU artifact generation.
domains.promptSnippet: Compile, check, and run Kain source files and projects
promptGuidelines: Use kain_lang when you need to compile Kain files to native code, run blades, check syntax/type correctness, or generate GPU shader artifacts.

check.label: Check
check.description: Run the Kain typechecker and semantic analysis on a file or directory without producing output. Set json:true for structured diagnostics.

build.label: Build
build.description: Compile a Kain file or project to a target backend: llvm, rust, cpp, wasm, spirv, cuda.

run.label: Run
run.description: Compile and execute a Kain file or project.

test.label: Test
test.description: Run Kain-language test fixtures and inline #[test] blocks.

amalgamate.label: Amalgamate
amalgamate.description: Amalgamate an entire blade workspace or folder into a single self-contained .kn file.

gpu_artifacts.label: GPU Artifacts
gpu_artifacts.description: Compile a shader .kn file to SPIR-V, PTX, or other GPU binary artifacts.

domains.name: Kain Native Compiler
domains.label: Kain Native
domains.description: Zero-friction native binary emitter: compile Kain to .exe, .dll, .lib, .obj in one command. Bridges kain build (LLVM IR) through bundled clang to produce native binaries. Auto-detects runtime dependencies and links accordingly.
domains.promptSnippet: Compile Kain source to native binaries (.exe, .dll, .lib, .obj) in one shot
promptGuidelines: Use kain_native to compile Kain source to native binaries without manual IR editing or clang invocation.
Default emit is 'exe' â€” produces a standalone executable next to the source file.
Use emit:'sharedlib' to produce a .dll/.so for FFI interop with Python, Node.js, Rust, C, etc.
The wrapper auto-detects whether the source needs libc and links accordingly.

build.label: Build
build.description: Compile a Kain .kn file to native binary. emit: exe(default), sharedlib, staticlib, object, llvm-ir. output: optional override path.

domains.name: Git
domains.label: Git
domains.description: Repository operations router â€” git status, diff (with per-file history context), commit log (scoped to file or folder), and a recent activity feed grouped by day with area breakdown. All actions operate on the current git working tree.
domains.promptSnippet: Repository operations: status, diff+history, log, recent activity
promptGuidelines: Use git for any git repository operations â€” checking status, showing diffs with context, browsing history, or seeing recent activity.
Use git action:'diff' for the 'what changed + why has it been changing' question â€” it pairs each diff hunk with recent history on the touched files.
Use git action:'recent' to see what's been changing across the repo, grouped by day with area breakdown (stdlib, crates, runtime, blades, â€¦).
Use git action:'log' path:'X:/crates/foo/' to browse commit history scoped to a specific file or folder.
Use git action:'status' for a quick branch + dirty + last-commit snapshot.

status.label: Status
status.description: Branch, last commit, dirty state (staged/unstaged/untracked counts). Quick health check.

diff.label: Diff
diff.description: Show working tree diff. For each touched file, also show recent history (last N commits touching it) so you know why it's been changing. Path scopes to a file/folder. staged:true shows staged changes. against:'main' diffs vs a ref.

log.label: Log
log.description: Show commit history. path scopes to a file/folder. limit caps the result (default 20). author and since filter the range.

recent.label: Recent
recent.description: Recent activity feed grouped by day with area breakdown. area filters to a top-level folder like 'crates' or 'stdlib'.

domains.name: Kain Binary Sync
domains.label: Kain Sync
domains.description: Sync the latest Bazel-built kain.exe/kn.exe to ~/.kain/bin/ so the compiler stays fresh. Uses 'bazel info output_base' to find the built binary, builds if missing, copies with backup, and verifies with 'kain doctor'.
domains.promptSnippet: Sync the latest Bazel-built Kain binary to ~/.kain/bin/
promptGuidelines: Use kain_sync_binary when the user reports stale binary issues, 'kain doctor' shows drift, or the compiler seems out of date.
If kain_sync_binary fails, read BAZEL.md for the full Bazel workflow, server lifecycle, and build/sync guide.

binary.label: Sync Binary
binary.description: Build (if needed) and copy the latest kain.exe + kn.exe from Bazel output to ~/.kain/bin/. Falls back with BAZEL.md guidance on failure.

status.label: Binary Status
status.description: Show when kain.exe was last built, its age, Bazel server state, git HEAD, and sync stamp info â€” all in one place.

search.label: Search Tools

domains.name: Oracle UI Validator
domains.label: Oracle
domains.description: Gaslight-proof Windows UI validator — queries the OS directly via Win32 P/Invoke + BitBlt + SendInput to find windows, capture screenshots, inject real input, and verify UI state changes. Returns structured JSON telemetry that no LLM can fake. Use after ANY kain build/kain_native that produces a .exe to prove the app actually works.
domains.promptSnippet: Gaslight-proof Windows UI validator: find windows, capture screenshots, inject input, verify UI state
promptGuidelines: Use oracle after ANY kain build / kain_native / bazel build that produces a Kain .exe — verification is mandatory, not optional.
The canonical workflow: scan → launch → debug → find → matrix → verify → delta. Never skip a step.
oracle scan --dir <project> to find the freshest .exe; oracle launch <exe> --wait 3000 to start it.
oracle debug --pid <pid> to diagnose why a process didn't create a GUI window (rejection reasons: TERMINAL, INVISIBLE, ZERO_SIZE).
oracle matrix --handle 0xN --text to mathematically prove the window is rendering (all zeros = black screen = FAIL).
oracle verify --handle 0xN --do 'click:X,Y' --expect 'pixels>100' for end-to-end UI interaction proof.
oracle delta --handle 0xN to prove the render loop is alive (frozen = dead).
If any step fails, STOP — never claim a Kain app works from console output alone. Report the Oracle JSON evidence.

scan.label: Scan for .exe
scan.description: Find the most recently built .exe files in a directory tree. Use after kain build to locate the output binary.

launch.label: Launch .exe
launch.description: Start an executable and return its PID. Optional --wait ms, --args, --cwd, --find (auto-locate window after launch).

debug.label: Debug Window Creation
debug.description: Show ALL windows a process created and WHY each was rejected. Verdict tells you if it's a console app, hidden, or crashed.

find.label: Find Window
find.description: Locate a valid GUI window by title keyword, PID, or process name. Polls until timeout with configurable interval.

info.label: Window Info
info.description: Full OS-level metadata for a window: handle, title, class, dimensions, position, PID, process name, visibility.

capture.label: Capture Screenshot
capture.description: Take a PNG screenshot of a window using BitBlt+CAPTUREBLT (captures windowed GPU content). Optionally client-area only.

matrix.label: Pixel Matrix
matrix.description: Generate a brightness (0-9) or color hex grid of the window. All zeros = black screen = app not rendering. Mathematical proof, not visual guesswork.

click.label: Click
click.description: Inject a real OS-level left mouse click at window client coordinates via SendInput.

type.label: Type Text
type.description: Inject real OS-level keystrokes (Unicode) into a window via SendInput.

delta.label: Frame Delta
delta.description: Capture two frames N ms apart and diff them. Proves whether the render loop is alive or frozen.

verify.label: Verify UI
verify.description: End-to-end UI proof: execute action (click/type), wait, capture before/after, diff, check expectation. E.g. prove a button click changed the UI.

kill.label: Kill Process
kill.description: Kill a process by PID or keyword match.

list.label: List All Windows
list.description: Enumerate all visible non-terminal GUI windows on the system with handles and metadata.

help.label: Help
help.description: Print full usage reference with all commands and examples.

domains.name: Z3 Solver (MCP)
domains.label: Z3
domains.description: Router for the locally-installed z3-mcp server (uv tool install X:/mcp/polytools/z3-mcp). Spawns the `z3-mcp` stdio JSON-RPC server on first call, keeps it alive for the session, and forwards each action to the matching MCP tool. Covers source analysis, SMT-LIB v2 checking, structured proof cases, proof-pack admin, and counterexample-to-regression-test scaffolding.
domains.promptSnippet: Solver-backed proof authoring: analyze source, check SMT2, run structured proofs, scaffold regression tests
promptGuidelines: Use z3 action:'check' for raw SMT-LIB v2 input (smt2 string, optional timeout_ms).
Use z3 action:'prove' for structured proof cases (kind + case dict, e.g. size_add_ok, range_check, state_machine_check).
Use z3 action:'analyze' to scan a source file (path, optional symbol/line) and surface proof opportunities.
Use z3 action:'extract' to materialize proof cases from a source file (path, optional symbol/line, save=true to write to a pack).
Use z3 action:'admin' for low-frequency ops: init_proof_pack, list_templates, discover_proof_packs, etc. (action + payload dict).
Use z3 action:'regress' to turn a Z3 counterexample into a regression test skeleton (template, counterexample, test_name?).
All actions accept an opaque `args` object that the z3-mcp server validates â€” when in doubt, call z3 action:'admin' with action='list_templates' first to see what kinds/cases are available.

Forward slashes in paths on Windows (X:/mcp/...). The server requires Z3_MCP_ROOT and Z3_MCP_POLYTOOLS_ROOT env vars, which the extension sets automatically from Z3_MCP_ROOT and Z3_MCP_POLYTOOLS_ROOT env vars (with sensible defaults).

analyze.label: Analyze Source
analyze.description: Analyze a source file for proof opportunities. args: { path, symbol?, line?, context_lines?, max_findings?, max_bytes?, debug? }. Forwards to MCP tool analyze_source_file.

extract.label: Extract Proof Cases
extract.description: Extract structured proof cases from a source file. args: { path, symbol?, line?, context_lines?, max_findings?, max_bytes?, save?, overwrite?, pack_path?, debug? }. Forwards to MCP tool extract_source_proof_cases.

check.label: Check SMT2
check.description: Run Z3 on raw SMT-LIB v2 input. args: { smt2, timeout_ms?, include_model?, include_stats?, project_root?, report_name? }. Forwards to MCP tool check_smt2. Returns { status: sat|unsat|unknown, model?, stats? }.

prove.label: Run Proof
prove.description: Run a structured proof case via the DSL. args: { kind, case, timeout_ms?, project_root?, report_name? }. Forwards to MCP tool prove. Use kind from the helper catalog (size_add_ok, size_mul_ok, ptr_offset_ok, content_length_ok, buffer_growth_ok, signed_unsigned_cast_ok, range_check, bitvec_equiv, state_machine_check, optimize, find_counterexample).

admin.label: Admin (tool_router)
admin.description: Low-frequency admin actions via the MCP tool_router. args: { action, payload? }. Actions include: init_proof_pack, run_proof_pack, list_templates, suggest_proof_targets, coverage_report, query_proof_inventory, materialize_proof_candidates, automate_proof_candidates, discover_proof_packs, discover_proof_plugins, init_proof_plugin, install_proof_plugin, read_proof_plugin, run_workspace_proofs, how_to_use, claim_proof_task, proof_task_list, save_proof_case, save_proof_case_to_pack, read_proof_pack, inventory_pack_symbols.

regress.label: Counterexample â†’ Test
regress.description: Turn a Z3 counterexample into a regression test skeleton. args: { template, counterexample, test_name?, function_name?, language?, output_path?, context? }. language defaults to 'c'. Forwards to MCP tool counterexample_to_test.
